text:
Ashley Rivera: heads up — running a quick thought experiment on per-org burst handling. what if we split burst credits into short buckets + a sampled SLA telemetry stream instead of global counters?
Matt Chen: curious, what problems are we solving specifically?
Ashley Rivera: current issues: a single large burst from one tenant can exhaust global short-window tokens and spike tail latencies for others. debugging is painful because the alerting just says "rate limit triggered".
Ivan Petrov: sounds like isolation + observability. how do buckets differ from existing burst credits?
Ashley Rivera: idea: each org gets N "micro-buckets" (e.g., 5s windows) that refill independently. we still keep a longer-term budget (RPM/TPM) but the short buckets prevent one huge fanout from bleeding past the short SLOs.
Sara Lee: micro-buckets could help smooth backpressure. how do we allocate N? fixed? dynamic?
Ashley Rivera: start fixed per tier (free=2, basic=4, enterprise=8) then autoscale based on sustained working set size / historical peak.
Matt Chen: autoscaling buckets worries me — more complexity in router. can we implement as an admission layer config instead of per-shard state?
Ivan Petrov: router can use a consistent hash to pick a bucket id per request (org_id -> shard -> bucket idx). minimal state if bucket refill is time-based and deterministic.
Kelly O'Neil: need to think about fairness for cross-region routing. if requests land in different routers, how do we avoid double-spend of same micro-bucket?
Ashley Rivera: plan: make micro-buckets eventually-consistent short-window local reserves + a global meter that enforces RPM/TPM. local routers serve from the local bucket first; if empty, consult global token service (fast path) or reject. sync via periodic reconciliation to avoid drift.
Sara Lee: what about telemetry? we need to know which constraint fired (local bucket vs global RPM) for product pages and SRE.
Ashley Rivera: exactly — propose sampled SLA telemetry that tags a subset of requests with enforcement_reason and bucket_idx. store in traces/metrics along with route, model, and token counts. 1% sample should be enough but allow on-demand 100% for specific orgs.
Matt Chen: sample-rate toggle in console would be nice for support debug. can we tie to rollouts so we can enable for a single org?
Ashley Rivera: yes, console toggle per org + operation window. UI needs to show recent enforcement events and which bucket fired.
Ivan Petrov: corner case — long-running streaming chats that keep KV cache and open sockets. we should count concurrency separately and not drain micro-buckets for every keepalive.
Kelly O'Neil: agreed. concurrency caps should be a separate dimension: N concurrent requests per org per region. keepalive extension should be charged differently (heartbeat vs new token).
Sara Lee: pinging quota-bot to propose schema changes for metrics: quota-bucket-id, enforcement_reason, local_router_id, sampled_trace_id.
quota-bot: created ticket Q-4123: "micro-bucket telemetry + enforcement_reason" — assigned to @Ivan Petrov, priority P2. https://tickets.example/redwood/Q-4123
Matt Chen: one more thought — how do retries interact? clients often retry immediately and can hammer other local buckets. need backoff guidance and possibly short blacklist on local bucket misses.
Ashley Rivera: good call. propose 100ms jittered backoff recommended in SDK and router-level exponential backoff when local bucket misses exceed threshold.
Ivan Petrov: next steps: prototype deterministic local buckets in the router (purely time-windowed), add sampled enforcement_reason telemetry, and a console toggle for per-org sampling. I'll pick up the router prototype this sprint.
Kelly O'Neil: i'll draft the console mockups and include a small panel listing recent enforcement events with links to traces.
Sara Lee: ops: we'll want an alert when local rejections spike > 0.5% of requests across a region for 5m.
Ashley Rivera: thanks all. keeping this small and reversible. marking for eng-platform sync tomorrow. :thumbsup:
